note.explanation: A solution is unsaturated if it can still dissolve more solute at a particular temperature. It is saturated when it has dissolved the maximum amount of solute possible in a particular amount of solvent at that temperature.
examples: Sugar dissolves in water, and more sugar can still dissolve: the solution is unsaturated.
At 20°C, 36 g of sodium chloride dissolves in 100 g of water to make a saturated solution.
note.checkAnswer: An unsaturated solution can dissolve more solute at that temperature; a saturated solution has dissolved the maximum amount.
note.simple: Unsaturated means more solute can dissolve. Saturated means no more can dissolve at that temperature.
note.checkQuestion: What is the difference between an unsaturated solution and a saturated solution?
note.title: Unsaturated and Saturated Solutions
steps: Check whether more solute can dissolve at the same temperature.
If more can dissolve, the solution is unsaturated.
If the maximum amount has dissolved, the solution is saturated.
note.answer: An unsaturated solution can dissolve more solute; a saturated solution contains the maximum amount that can dissolve at that temperature.

written.text: Why do different compounds have different solubilities in water at a particular temperature?
written.finalAnswer: Different compounds have different solubilities because their particles differ; the section explains that larger sugar molecules can be surrounded by more water molecules than salt ions, so more sugar dissolves.

written.text: Define solubility of a solute. How does the solubility of solutes change with the increase in temperature?
written.finalAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution. The effect of increasing temperature depends on the solute; the solubility of most solids in water increases, while that of gases generally decreases.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution.
The effect of an increase in temperature depends on the solute.
The solubility of most solid solutes in water increases with temperature, whereas the solubility of gases generally decreases.

Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent at a particular temperature; most solids become more soluble as temperature rises, while gases generally become less soluble.

steps.why: This sets up the solvent and solute amounts used in the textbook's demonstration.
steps.text: Take about 100 g of water in a beaker, add to it 5g of table sugar, and stir it.

steps.why: A further addition dissolves too, showing that the solution can still take in more solute.
steps.text: Then add another 5g of sugar and stir. This will also dissolve.

steps.why: The solution is unsaturated because it can still dissolve more sugar at that temperature.
steps.text: This solution is called an unsaturated solution.

steps.why: This gives the textbook's definition and identifies the key condition: the particular temperature.
steps.text: A solution which can dissolve more amount of a solute at a particular temperature is called an unsaturated solution.

example.question: In the textbook's sugar-and-water demonstration, how can you tell that the solution is unsaturated?
example.answer: The added sugar dissolves, and the solution can dissolve more solute at that temperature, so it is unsaturated.

explain.title: Unsaturated solution
explain.body: A solution which can dissolve more amount of a solute at a particular temperature is called an unsaturated solution. The key test is whether more solute can still dissolve.

explain.title: Saturated solution
explain.body: A solution in which the maximum amount of the solute has been dissolved in a particular amount of a solvent at a particular temperature is called a saturated solution. At that temperature, extra solute will not dissolve and may settle at the bottom.

explain.title: Solubility can differ
explain.body: Different solutes have different solubilities in the same solvent. At 20°C, 36 g of sodium chloride dissolves in 100 g of water to give a saturated solution, while 203.9 g of table sugar dissolves in water to give its saturated solution.

explain.title: Why sugar dissolves in a larger amount
explain.body: The section explains that sugar molecules are larger than salt ions. More water molecules can surround a single sugar molecule, causing sugar to dissolve in larger amounts.

mistakes: Leaving out “at a particular temperature” when defining either kind of solution.
Calling a solution unsaturated just because it is dilute, without checking whether more solute can dissolve.
Confusing the amount of water with the amount of solute in the 20°C comparison.
Saying that no solute is present in a saturated solution; saturation means the maximum amount has dissolved, not that the solution contains no solute.
